egress.terms: Free anonymous access without login. Endpoint GET /api/access/datafile/<id> returns HTTP 303 to a signed S3 URL with 1-hour expiration, supporting Range requests.

tooling: REST native API (create dataset, add files, direct S3 upload), plus the official Python/CLI clients. dataset count 306,027 live. rclone has no native backend but the S3 direct-upload path accepts any S3 client.
chaining: Collection creation is open to any logged-in user. The quota endpoint returns a 1 TiB allocation (1,099,511,627,776 bytes) for some collections and no quota for others, so a per-collection allocation is not shown for every collection.

notes: 1 TB per Dataverse Collection allocation (2.5 TB for Harvard affiliates). Per-file 2.5 GB through UI/API; larger via the S3 direct-upload path. The 1 TB is enforced as a *collection* allocation, not a per-person cap: GET /api/dataverses/<alias>/storage/quota?showInherited=true returns {"Total quota allocation for this collection": 1099511627776} for ordinary collections, and one live collection returns 2748779069440 (2.5 TB).

extras.egress_verbatim: Free, anonymous, no login: GET /api/access/datafile/<id> returns 303 to a signed dvn-cloud-iqss S3 URL (X-Amz-Expires=3600), which serves 200 with Content-Length and honours Range (206 + Content-Range). Tested live this session.
extras.chaining_verbatim: This is the wave-8 correction: quota attaches to the COLLECTION, and any logged-in user can create collections again since June 2024 (restriction imposed Nov 2022 in IQSS/dataverse.harvard.edu#199 was lifted; #207 comment 2024-07-24: 'Anyone can create collections in Harvard Dataverse now, as of sometime in June 2024'). N collections = N x 1 TiB allocations. Sibling collections can also be nested, so a 'Dataverse Collection' tree is the natural shard key.
extras.tooling_verbatim: REST native API (create dataset, add files, direct S3 upload), plus the official Python/CLI clients. dataset count 306,027 live. rclone has no native backend but the S3 direct-upload path accepts any S3 client.
extras.agent_focus: Bulk data programmes that pay for your storage. Two halves: (1) institutional/gov repositories and cloud open-data sponsorships, judged as free byte pools; (2) research grants that could fund storage for an unaffiliated individual. Revisited AWS ODS, Google Cloud public datasets, Source Cooperative. Central question for each: what is the unit of quota (account / record / dataset / collection / project), because that unit is the multiplier.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
